changes.name: Removed 'rate' property from rate-limit response
changes.description: The `rate` property was removed from the JSON body of the rate-limit response. Rate limit information is now provided via `resources.core.remaining` and `resources.core.reset` in the JSON body. GitHub also recommends `x-ratelimit-*` response headers for real-time tracking, treating them as authoritative when they disagree with the endpoint response.
changes.old_behavior: Code reading `rate_limit_json['rate']['remaining']` or `rate.remaining` from the response body
changes.migration: Update code to read `resources.core.remaining` and `resources.core.reset` from the JSON response body instead of `rate.remaining` and `rate.reset`.
changes.verified_impact: Repositories that parse the rate-limit response JSON for `rate.remaining` will receive a complete rate limit object without the `rate` key, potentially causing KeyError or incorrect limit calculations.

changes.name: Repository contents submodule type change
changes.description: Submodules in the repository contents are now returned with `type='submodule'` instead of `type='file'`. Directories have `type='dir'`, and regular files have `type='file'.
changes.old_behavior: Code assuming every directory entry has `type == 'file'` when listing repository contents; git commands parsing the contents response may misidentify submodules as files
changes.migration: Always check the `type` field before assuming the entry type; submodules have `type='submodule'` with `content.sha` pointing to the submodule commit, while files have `type='file'` with `content` containing the file content (base64-encoded)
changes.verified_impact: Repositories that iterate contents and treat every entry as a file will incorrectly attempt to decode submodule entries as file content, potentially causing base64 decoding errors or missing submodule metadata.

changes.name: Workflow dispatch response changed from 204 to 200
changes.description: The workflow dispatch endpoint now returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON body containing a `create_status` URL, instead of returning 204 No Content. The response body includes details about the queued workflow run.
changes.old_behavior: Code checking `response.status_code == 204` after workflow dispatch; assuming immediate effect without polling the create_status URL
changes.migration: Expect HTTP 200 response; parse the `create_status` URL from the response body to check the workflow run status instead of assuming 204 means immediate queue
changes.verified_impact: Code that explicitly checks for 204 and proceeds without waiting for the workflow to be processed may miss the queued run or fail to track its status correctly.
